done.why: The duel with my own double ended, the figure faded and I took its cloak. It felt like a natural stopping point.

about: A dreamlike cave adventure. A silver-haired man says I must prove myself worthy. I found a lantern, wandered shadowy lands, and fought a hooded figure who turned out to be me.

ending.what: I beat my hooded double, saw my own face, and took its cloak. I don't know whether that was the real ending or only one test.

moments.note: Pitch black and a warning about being eaten. I had no idea what to do until I tried turning on the lantern.
'Who do you think you are? Arthur?' The sword refused me.
Waiting made the figure appear, and the sword jumped into my hand by itself.
Removing the hood showed my own face, which then aged and faded. A strong moment.
I talked to the figure and it did not respond. I wasn't sure whether to fight or talk.

wished: A clearer sign of whether I should fight or talk to the figure.
To know what the final test actually was.
To look at my own wounds or what I carried.

lines.line: The footsteps stop, off in the hills, as if somebody were listening
lines.why: It hinted at how to meet the figure without being a command.

lines.line: recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded
lines.why: This was the emotional peak of the game.

fun.why: The duel was exciting and had a good twist.

engagement.why: The footsteps pulled me forward, and the fight had momentum.

difficulty.why: Mostly clear. The dark room and the figure were slightly puzzling.

interestingness.why: Fighting a mirror self and then sparing it was a fresh idea.

prose.why: Atmospheric and economical, with some strong lines.
